prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a town where Jesus, Paul or Barnabas taught or preached in a synagogue
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a town where Jesus, Paul or Barnabas taught or preached in a synagogue
prompts.summary: Jesus began his public ministry by reading Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue. Paul followed the same pattern on his missions, going first to the Jews: Damascus right after his conversion, Salamis on Cyprus, Antioch in Pisidia and Iconium, then Thessalonica, Berea, Athens, Corinth and Ephesus.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jesus read Isaiah in the synagogue at Nazareth and taught in the synagogue at Capernaum (Luke 4:16; Mark 1:21).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul reasoned in synagogues at Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and Corinth (Acts 17:1-2, 10, 17; 18:4).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul and Barnabas spoke in synagogues at Antioch in Pisidia and Iconium; Paul later at Ephesus (Acts 13:14; 14:1; 19:8).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Straightway after his conversion Saul preached Christ in the synagogues of Damascus (Acts 9:20).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: At Salamis, Barnabas and Saul preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews (Acts 13:5).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory Gordon B. Hinckley visited on his May 1996 Asia trip
prompts.text_original: In May 1996 President Gordon B. Hinckley toured Asia, dedicating the Hong Kong China Temple and offering prayers in Cambodia and Vietnam. A country or territory on that trip.
prompts.citation: Ensign, August 1996, News of the Church
prompts.summary: In May 1996 Gordon B. Hinckley met Saints across East Asia: Japan, Korea, Taiwan and the Philippines. He dedicated the Hong Kong China Temple, stopped in Shenzhen, dedicated Cambodia for preaching and prayed in Hanoi. Even a refueling stop on Saipan became a meeting with members.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: He dedicated the Hong Kong China Temple, May 26-27.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Tokyo, Osaka, Fukuoka and Naha, Okinawa.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: A stop in Shenzhen.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Pusan and Seoul.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Manila and Cebu.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Taipei.

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: In Phnom Penh he dedicated Cambodia for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Northern Mariana Islands
answers.fact: A refueling stop on Saipan, where he met members.

answers.name: Vietnam
answers.fact: Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, where he offered an addendum prayer.

prompts.display_text: Pin a British Commonwealth country whose Latter-day Saint servicemen fought in the early Allied operations of World War II.
prompts.text_original: Latter-day Saint servicemen from several British Commonwealth countries took part in the early Allied military operations of World War II. Pin one of those countries.
prompts.citation: Church History Topics: World War II
prompts.summary: The United States did not enter World War II until December 1941. Before then, Church History Topics notes, Latter-day Saint servicemen from Great Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa were already taking part in Allied operations.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Great Britain is named; it declared war on Germany in September 1939.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Named among the countries whose Saints served early in the war.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Named among the countries whose Saints served early in the war.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Named among the countries whose Saints served early in the war.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Named among the countries whose Saints served early in the war.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a dedicated temple named for its capital and another named for a different city (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country with a dedicated temple named for its national capital and another dedicated temple named for a different city (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Thirteen countries have a dedicated temple named for the capital and at least one named for another city, from the United States and Mexico to Colombia, Ecuador, Honduras and the United Kingdom. Canada, Australia and South Africa have several temples but none in their capitals, and New Zealand's Wellington temple is still under construction.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Mexico City 1983 plus thirteen more.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Washington D.C. Temple (1974, in nearby Maryland) plus temples nationwide.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Brasília 2023 plus São Paulo and others.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Lima 1986 plus Trujillo and Arequipa.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Buenos Aires 1986 plus Córdoba, Mendoza, Salta, Bahía Blanca.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Santiago 1983 plus Concepción and Antofagasta.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala City 1984 plus Quetzaltenango and Cobán.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Tokyo 1980 plus Fukuoka, Sapporo, Okinawa.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Manila 1984 plus Cebu City, Urdaneta and others.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Bogotá 1999 plus Barranquilla 2018.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Quito 2022 plus Guayaquil 1999.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London 1958 plus Preston 1998.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: Tegucigalpa 2013 plus San Pedro Sula 2024.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology names a local member as a translator or reviewer of the Book of Mormon.
prompts.text_original: The Church's country chronologies often name local members, rather than foreign missionaries, who translated or reviewed the Book of Mormon in their own language. Pin a country whose chronology names one of its own members in that role.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Denmark, France, Germany, Sweden, Netherlands, Spain, Hungary, Russia, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Hawaii, Thailand, Armenia
prompts.summary: From the start, converts carried the Book of Mormon into their own languages: Peter Olsen Hansen into Danish, Louis Bertrand into French, Jonathan Napela into Hawaiian, August Carlson into Swedish. In the 1900s local members led translations in Thailand, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Russia, Hungary and Armenia.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Peter Olsen Hansen, brother of one of the first Danish converts, translated into Danish, published 1851.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: George Viett, a German convert baptized in Paris, helped translate into German in 1851-52.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Louis A. Bertrand, an early Paris convert, translated the Book of Mormon into French.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: John W. F. Volker translated the Book of Mormon into Dutch, published 1890.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: August W. Carlson translated the Book of Mormon into Swedish in 1878.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Jonathan H. Napela, a Hawaiian convert, translated into Hawaiian with George Q. Cannon from 1852.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: Lead translators Brikena Ribaj and Juventila Sinamati produced the Albanian Book of Mormon, available in Tirana in November 1999.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Meliton Gonzalez Trejo, a Spaniard, was one of the main translators of the 1886 Spanish edition.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Priscilla Sampson-Davis of Accra translated the Book of Mormon and other Church materials into Fante.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: A translation committee of local members began the Chinese translation in 1957.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Stuart Meha and William Duncan Sr. worked with Matthew Cowley to revise the Maori Book of Mormon in 1917-19.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Andre Anastasion, who joined the Church in 1918, began the Russian translation in the 1920s.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Srilaksana Suntarahut, a Thai convert, was the principal translator of the 1976 Thai edition.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: The Chinese Book of Mormon published in Taipei on November 2, 1963, came through the efforts of Hu Wei-i.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: Andre Anastasion, a native of Odesa, began translating the Book of Mormon into Russian in 1925.

answers.name: Armenia
answers.fact: Four Armenian members served as the ecclesiastical review team for the Eastern Armenian edition in 2000.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Evangeline Kokotanova Coy, a Bulgarian convert, produced the first manuscript Bulgarian translation of the Book of Mormon in 1934.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: Maria Salas Calvo translated selections of the Book of Mormon into CHamoru, available in book form in 1989.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Etus von Haragos, a Hungarian member, worked on the Hungarian translation from 1931.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Sveinbjorg Gudmundsdottir and Halldor Hansen translated the Icelandic Book of Mormon, published in Reykjavik in 1977.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: A translation team including Dorothy Tembo, George Murenza and Moses Murahwa produced the Shona triple combination, published 2007.
